clusters.label: Naive Bayes Classifier Core
clusters.rationale: These candidates all describe the fundamental Naive Bayes algorithm as a probabilistic classifier using Bayes theorem and the naive independence assumption.

clusters.label: Bayes Theorem and Probability Foundations
clusters.rationale: These candidates cover probability basics, conditional probability, and Bayes theorem, which are the mathematical underpinnings necessary for understanding Naive Bayes.

clusters.label: Feature Independence and Multicollinearity
clusters.rationale: These candidates discuss the naive assumption of feature independence and the related issue of multicollinearity, explaining why the algorithm is called 'naive'.

clusters.label: Naive Bayes Algorithm Variants
clusters.rationale: These candidates present the three main variants of Naive Bayes (Bernoulli, Multinomial, Gaussian) and their respective use cases.

clusters.label: Zero Frequency Error and Laplace Smoothing
clusters.rationale: These candidates address the zero frequency probability problem in Naive Bayes and the Laplace smoothing technique to mitigate it.

clusters.label: Naive Bayes Applications and Usage Guidance
clusters.rationale: These candidates describe practical applications of Naive Bayes, its advantages, disadvantages, and guidelines on when to use it.

clusters.label: Improving Naive Bayes Performance
clusters.rationale: These candidates provide tips and techniques to enhance Naive Bayes performance, including feature engineering and log-trick for numerical stability.

clusters.label: Gaussian Naive Bayes Mathematical Details
clusters.rationale: These candidates detail the Gaussian Naive Bayes model, including the Gaussian PDF formula, calculation of prior and class conditional probabilities, and the log-trick.

clusters.label: Naive Bayes Training and Prediction Procedure
clusters.rationale: These candidates describe the step-by-step process of training (computing per-class statistics) and prediction (posterior calculation and argmax) in Naive Bayes.

clusters.label: Naive Bayes Implementation in Python
clusters.rationale: These candidates outline the Python implementation of a Naive Bayes classifier, including class structure, methods, and testing.

clusters.label: Sentiment Analysis Definition and Labeled Data
clusters.rationale: These candidates introduce sentiment analysis as a text classification task and emphasize the necessity of labeled data.

clusters.label: Bag-of-Words Model
clusters.rationale: These candidates explain the bag-of-words representation in text analytics, converting text into word frequency vectors.

clusters.label: Naive Bayes Decision Rule Derivation
clusters.rationale: These candidates derive the Naive Bayes decision rule mathematically, from Bayes theorem to the final classification formula.

clusters.label: Training Components: Prior and Likelihood
clusters.rationale: These candidates cover the calculation of prior class probabilities and word likelihood probabilities during Naive Bayes training.

clusters.label: Smoothing and Logarithmic Transformation
clusters.rationale: These candidates address Laplace smoothing and log transformation for numerical stability in Naive Bayes.

clusters.label: Text Preprocessing for NLP
clusters.rationale: These candidates describe text cleaning steps such as removing HTML, punctuation, stop words, lowercasing, tokenization, and stemming.

clusters.label: Binary Multinomial Naive Bayes
clusters.rationale: These candidates discuss a variant of Naive Bayes that uses binary features indicating word presence rather than frequency.

clusters.label: Handling Unknown Words and Vocabulary
clusters.rationale: These candidates cover strategies for dealing with out-of-vocabulary words and building vocabularies with frequency filters.

clusters.label: IMDb Dataset Details and Loading
clusters.rationale: These candidates describe the IMDb movie review dataset and the process of downloading and extracting it.

clusters.label: Reading and Tokenizing IMDb Reviews
clusters.rationale: These candidates explain how to read reviews from files and tokenize them into words.

clusters.label: Sequence Padding and Data Iterators
clusters.rationale: These candidates discuss padding/truncating sequences and creating data iterators for minibatch training.

clusters.label: Data Loading Pipeline Encapsulation
clusters.rationale: These candidates present a reusable function that bundles all data preprocessing steps for the IMDb dataset.

clusters.label: NLP Definition and Context
clusters.rationale: These candidates define natural language processing and its role in text classification tasks.

clusters.label: Feature Extraction with CountVectorizer and BoW
clusters.rationale: These candidates illustrate using CountVectorizer to create bag-of-words representations, similar to the BoW model.

clusters.label: Model Application: MultinomialNB for Sentiment
clusters.rationale: These candidates demonstrate applying Multinomial Naive Bayes for text classification using scikit-learn.

clusters.label: Model Evaluation and Splitting
clusters.rationale: These candidates cover train/test splitting, accuracy evaluation, and model persistence.

clusters.label: Evaluation Metrics for Classification
clusters.rationale: These candidates introduce metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix.

clusters.label: Hyperparameter Tuning with GridSearchCV
clusters.rationale: These candidates describe using GridSearchCV for hyperparameter tuning in Naive Bayes.

clusters.label: Imbalanced Class Distribution
clusters.rationale: These candidates discuss the impact of imbalanced data on classification tasks.
